name: Shade beats air temperature
text: In hot, sunny places, how hot people feel outdoors depends more on radiant heat from the sun and surfaces than on air temperature. Shade from buildings cooled most by day in a Tempe study, then trees, then light structures.

source.label: Middel et al., 50 Grades of Shade

name: Reflective paving can make walking hotter
text: In Los Angeles, coated roads were up to 6 °C cooler on the surface, but pedestrians above them received about 4 °C more radiant heat. Pair reflective surfaces with shade.

name: Misting depends on humidity and air movement
text: In Singapore, a misting fan cut air temperature by about 1.5 °C and made people feel cooler. An overhead misting line without fans made no significant difference.

name: Trees cool people more than thermometers show
text: WRI’s Cool Cities Lab puts the improvement trees make to thermal comfort at roughly 2–8 °C. That measures how hot people feel, which is not the same as air temperature.

source.label: World Resources Institute: Urban trees, an underused tool for keeping people cool
